body:
**Audit — routing corrected from a domain lane to an epic lane.**

Maintainer, 2026-08-17, verbatim:

> 测试卡不是应该你同意认领统一执行吗？怎么被派到 devx 车道

Correct, and the mislabel had teeth. I had put `domain:devx` on the wave's run cards (#9298, #9300, #9301, #9302, #9303) and on #9308. `domain:*` is a **lane-ownership** label: it offers a card to that seat's queue. #9300–9303 are unassigned by design (they are blocked on #9298), so the moment the unlock scan flipped them back to `pm:queue`, the devx seat could have claimed a round entirely legitimately — and run it with its own runners, its own tree, and whatever `main` looked like at that hour. Every round in this wave has to run against **one** pinned baseline in **one** provisioned tree; a second seat taking a round would have split the baseline while both halves still called themselves the same full regression. That is a silent corruption of the run record, not a cosmetic slip.

Two things were wrong, not one:

1. **Wrong mechanism.** The protocol already has the right shape for a subtree owned by one PM session — `pm:epic` on the parent plus the session ID and declared territory in the body, which makes other PMs skip the whole subtree when gathering candidates. That is now in place.
2. **Wrong producer.** `domain:*` is the triage seat's single-producer output. An execution session on the direct-dispatch channel does not mint lane labels. The precedent I leaned on (#7671, #7687, #7740) does not transfer: those are checklist-maintenance **code PRs**, which genuinely are devx lane work. A QA run produces a run record and no code, so it belongs to no domain lane at all.

Applied and read back:

| card | labels now |
|---|---|
| #9296 | `tracking`, `tests`, **`pm:epic`** |
| #9298 | `tests`, `pm:dispatched` |
| #9300 / #9301 / #9302 / #9303 | `tests`, `pm:blocked` |
| #9308 | `tests`, `pm:queue` — domain label removed; **triage routes this one**, it is a real code card in `examples/app-showcase` and not mine to lane |
| #9299 | `tests`, `pm:dispatched`, `domain:devx` — **deliberately unchanged**: it edits `docs/qa/platform-checklist/**` and produced PR #9309, which is exactly what the devx lane owns |

`tests` stays on all of them — it is a topic label, not a lane.

**Board simplification — closed the four per-round scaffolding cards (#9300, #9301, #9302, #9303) as not planned.**

Maintainer, 2026-08-17, verbatim:

> 你还没开始测试就需要创建这么多卡吗？

No. Nine cards were filed on this wave and **zero checklist items had been executed**. Four of them were pure scaffolding and are now closed.

**Why they were redundant.** A round's spec is `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs <selector> --json` — deterministic, versioned, and already the authority the runner is required to obey. A round's *record* is the `qa-run` issue the runner files when it finishes, per the standing rule at the top of this card: one selector, one run, one issue. A pre-filed card for the same round adds a third artifact carrying no information the other two lack, so each round cost two issues, one of which was ceremony.

**Why filing them was a mistake and not just noise.** The claim/dispatch/review ceremony in the PM protocol exists because many agents contend for one shared backlog. This wave has no contention: one session, one QA tree, one pinned baseline (`e4e5c6e3`), delegated as a `pm:epic` subtree that other seats skip. Transplanting the ceremony wholesale produced four unassigned cards sitting in a lane queue — which is exactly the collision hazard corrected in the previous comment. The ceremony did not protect anything here; it manufactured the risk it exists to prevent.

**What tracks the rounds now**: the round table in this card's body, plus the `qa-run` issue each round files on completion. **The 15 R3 area cards will not be filed** — same reasoning; each area's record is its own run issue.

Still open and unchanged: **#9298** (R0, in flight — it carries live readings and closing an in-flight card would discard them). #9299 is delivered. Reopening any of the four is free if a round ever does need its own claimable card — e.g. if a second seat is ever brought in to parallelize R3.

**R0 complete · R3 dispatched to three cloud sessions · actual testing starts now.**

## R0 (#9298) — the machine-lane baseline, and it is green

Full readings are on #9298. The headline: **the repo is green at the pinned sha** — `turbo run test --continue --concurrency=2` → 135/135 tasks, 72 test packages, **43,531 tests passed, 0 failed suites** (37m36s). `objectstack verify` against showcase: 15 verified, 0 gaps, 0 FAILED, 1 needs-fixture, 7 skipped. Boot smoke: health 200 in 10s, `/_console/` 200.

Corrections R0 made to my dispatch, both adopted:

- `--concurrency=2` alone was **not** enough — `@objectstack/types` still failed; it took `--concurrency=2 --continue` to get a complete reading. Nothing survives low concurrency, so #9311 needs no companion card.
- Its own dogfood failure was **self-inflicted** (it ran the golden suite beside the console build) and it said so rather than banking it as a defect. That is now a standing rule for R1–R3: never run a suite concurrently with a build.

Two red gates filed, neither fixed, neither a product defect: **#9307** (cold-tree console build ordering — pre-existing since 2026-07-02, self-heals on retry, which is why it has always read as flake) and **#9311** (two under-budgeted test timeouts).

**Console cost is now zero for every later local round** — the dist persists in the QA tree: 16.5 min cold, 8.5 min warm, paid once.

## R3 — three cloud sessions, not fifteen

Each cloud container must build its own console, so the split is by **cost of setup**, not by area count: three sessions, each running its areas sequentially, each paying the console build once. Fifteen sessions would have paid it fifteen times.

| session | areas | items |
|---|---|---|
| R3-A | records-forms · approvals · studio-authoring | 59 |
| R3-B | access-security · identity-auth · platform-core · integration-system | 61 |
| R3-C | api-backend · automation · dashboards · cli · attachments-storage · ai · search · i18n | 70 |

Each is pinned to the subject sha `e4e5c6e3`, carries #9307's workaround so it does not lose a round re-diagnosing a known bug, owns a private port band (3200 / 3300 / 3400), and files **one `qa-run` issue per area** as it finishes — 15 issues total, not one at the end, so progress survives an interruption.

R3-B additionally carries a **withhold rule**: a real access-control hole gets its clause marked `fail` with the reproduction withheld from the public issue and posted here for the maintainer instead.

## Subject pin vs test spec — recording the ruling

`main` has moved past the wave's pin (`e4e5c6e3` → `862eb1402` at the time of writing) and will keep moving; this repo merges continuously. A full regression against a moving target can never be "latest" — it can only be **one honest pin**. So:

- **Subject (code under test) stays pinned at `e4e5c6e3`.** That is what R0's gate readings, the console build, and every run record describe.
- **Spec (the checklist) advances**, via `git checkout origin/main -- docs/qa/platform-checklist/` in each runner's tree. PR #9309 is docs-only, so taking it does not move the subject by one byte, and run records already pin per-item `revision`.

## Still ahead

Local rounds in the QA tree once #9309 merges (it is green and clean; a branch update was pushed to give auto-merge a status event to fire on): `priority:P0` (18 items after the sweep), `surface:api`, `surface:cli`, `surface:build`. Those need no console and run on the now-idle box.

**Correction to the round plan: R2a/R2b/R2c are dropped, not merely un-carded. R1 is running.**

When #9301/#9302/#9303 were closed as scaffolding, each closing comment said the round "still runs as part of #9296". That is no longer true, and the record should not be left implying it.

**Why they were dropped.** R3 covers **all 15 areas in full** — 190 items. Every item a `surface:api`, `surface:cli` or `surface:build` selector would reach is therefore already inside some area run. Those three rounds were not a coverage layer; they were 62 duplicated item-runs and three extra run issues, on a box whose CPU is the wave's binding constraint. The plan was drawn before the cloud split made R3 exhaustive, and it should have been re-derived then rather than carried forward.

**Why R1 survives.** `priority:P0` is not a coverage layer either — it is a **latency** one. The three cloud sessions are ~40 minutes from their first verdict (clone, install, console build); the local tree is already provisioned, so P0 can answer "is anything release-blocking broken?" in minutes. Duplication that buys early warning on the release-gating set is worth it; duplication that buys a second copy of an ordinary verdict is not.

**R1 is dispatched now**, in the provisioned tree at `e4e5c6e3`, port band 3110–3129, max 3 items in parallel, per R0's measured conventions.

One deliberate deviation recorded for auditability: R1 takes the checklist from **PR #9309's head `d23a746c7`** (reviewed, accepted, sitting in the merge queue) rather than from `main`, so it runs the 18-item P0 set instead of the stale 16. The subject stays pinned at `e4e5c6e3`; only the spec moved, and per-item `revision` pinning makes exactly which spec it ran auditable. The cloud sessions take the same ledger from `main` once the queue lands it.

Round table as it now stands: **R0** ✅ · **R4** ✅ (in queue) · **R1** 🔄 running · **R2a/b/c** ❌ dropped as redundant · **R3** 🔄 three cloud sessions, 15 `qa-run` issues expected.

**R1 (`priority:P0`) — release-blocking FAIL found and twice-derived: `DELETE` is unconditionally broken for any object targeted by a `multiple: true` reference.**

Posting mid-round per the fast-fail contract. Subject `e4e5c6e3`, spec from PR #9309 head `fbd1c0491` (docs-only; byte-identical to `d23a746c7` under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`).

## The defect

`DELETE /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>` answers **400 `INVALID_FILTER`** and the row survives. The error names `f_lookups` — a field on a *different* object (`showcase_field_zoo`) — and instructs the caller to fix a filter the caller never sent.

Chain, each link independently evidenced:

1. The delete handler enumerates every field referencing the target object and probes each for dependents — `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:10112`:
   ```js
   dependents = await this.find(childName, { where: { [fieldName]: id }, context } as any);
   ```
   Bare equality, for **every** referencing field regardless of arity.
2. `showcase_field_zoo.f_lookups` is a multi-value reference to `showcase_account` (`examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts:106`, `Field.lookup('showcase_account', { multiple: true })`), stored as a JSON TEXT column.
3. The engine's own filter-shape guard (#5869, `filter-comparand-shape.ts`) refuses bare `=` on that column — the exact refusal the response quotes.
4. The `catch` directly below (#8895 hardening) rethrows anything that is not `isMissingTableError`, so the probe failure **aborts the delete**: `if (isMissingTableError(error)) continue; throw error;`

The #8895 fail-closed hardening is correct in itself; it converts a previously silent probe failure into a hard refusal, which is what makes this visible now. The bug is step 1 emitting a filter shape step 3 rejects — the remedy is the one the error message itself gives: `$contains` for multi-value fields.

## Reproduction rule

Fresh boot, no prior state:
```
pnpm -C examples/app-showcase exec objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 3112 -d file:/tmp/qa-wave/r1-del.db
POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email  {"email":"admin@objectos.ai","password":"admin123"}
GET  /api/v1/data/showcase_account?$top=50        → take the "Northwind" row id
DELETE /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>
```
- **expected**: 200, row gone.
- **actual**: `400 {"code":"INVALID_FILTER","object":"showcase_account","error":"The bare equality spelling { \"f_lookups\": value } WAS NOT APPLIED: \"f_lookups\" is a multi-value … field, stored by this driver as a JSON TEXT column … Use \"$contains\" …"}`, and a follow-up `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>` returns **200** — the row survives.

## Scope, measured not assumed

| object | DELETE | note |
|---|---|---|
| `showcase_account` | **400 `INVALID_FILTER`** | target of a `multiple: true` lookup |
| `showcase_team` / `showcase_category` / `showcase_announcement` / `showcase_private_note` / `showcase_project` | 200 | no multi-value referencing field |
| `showcase_product` | 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED` | correct referential guard, working as designed |
| `sys_user` | 405 `OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | delete not exposed on the data API, so the multi-value `Field.user` fields (`f_users`, `team_members`) never reach the probe |

On stock showcase the blast radius is exactly `showcase_account`. The framework-level rule is broader: **any** object that is the target of a `multiple: true` reference from a registered object is undeletable through the data API. `sys_user` escapes only because its delete verb is gated earlier.

## Rule-2 / rule-7 discipline paid

- Reproduced **6+ times across two independent boots** — port 3110 / `r1-core.db` and port 3112 / a freshly created `r1-del.db` — on distinct record ids including a seeded row. Not state-dependent.
- Automation self-check: driven with plain `curl -X DELETE`, no filter parameter sent; the offending filter is server-generated. No browser, so no `automation-input` / `hydration-race` exposure.
- Second, independent re-derivation performed from the captured traces + the three source locations alone, without reference to the first narrative — same conclusion.

Filed against this wave; item verdict `records-forms.crud-roundtrip` clause 2 = `fail`. It is a framework defect (`packages/objectql`), not a console one, so it stays in this repo.

Remaining R1 items continue; the full run issue follows at round end.

**R1 complete — run record filed as #9334.**

`priority:P0` · subject `e4e5c6e3` · spec PR #9309 head `fbd1c0491` · **7 PASS / 7 PARTIAL / 2 FAIL / 2 BLOCKED** across all 18 items.

The two P0 failures are the ones already posted above ([DELETE regression](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9296#issuecomment-5316926462), [unauthenticated datasource-admin family](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9296#issuecomment-5316955485)); #9334 carries the verdict tables, per-item revisions and the fixture gaps, with the access-control reproduction withheld to this card.

**Three things the later rounds should take from R1 before they burn time on them:**

1. **`objectstack verify --rls` is a separate invocation.** Bare `objectstack verify` — what R0 ran, and what I ran first — emits **no RLS section at all**; `runRlsProofs` only executes behind the flag. Any round citing plain `verify` as the oracle for an RLS clause has not consulted it. With the flag: 20 PROVEN, **0 HOLES**, 9/9 position personas.
2. **Playwright on this box needs an explicit `executablePath`.** `@playwright/test` 1.62.1 wants chromium build 1234; only `chromium-1194` is installed. The stock config reports **31 failed** — pure environment. With `launchOptions.executablePath=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome` it is **31 passed**. A cloud round that hits this and files it as a product defect will cost a full triage cycle.
3. **`?id=` on `/api/v1/meta/app` keys on the app NAME, not the package id.** `?id=com.example.showcase` returns `{"items":[]}`, which reads exactly like "the app metadata is gone". The real names are `showcase_app` / `setup` / `studio` / `account`. The checklist and the dogfood skill §1 both carry the wrong spelling — five checklist-accuracy findings are itemised in #9334 for whoever owns the ledger next.

Two items are unscoreable on stock showcase and should not be re-attempted without new fixtures: **`no-active-org-session-semantics`** (deployment is `tenancy: single`, so ADR-0095 Layer 0 is inert and every clause is vacuous — the runtime log says so outright, and the item's own unit pin contains a control asserting exactly that) and **`studio-authoring.first-run-loop`** (Studio is not installed in the showcase; the admin's app list is `["showcase_app","setup","account"]`).

Environment left clean: all instances stopped, probe rows and probe datasources removed, `git status` shows only `docs/qa/**`, nothing committed.

**R3-C interim status — 2 of 8 areas filed, both partial-scope. Not a completion summary.**

Filing this rather than going quiet: R3-C did not get through its eight areas in one session, and the two run records it did file are explicitly scoped at less than their full areas. Titles and bodies say so; neither claims "FULL area".

| area | items | filed | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| api-backend | **8 of 14** | #9333 | 4 PASS / 4 PARTIAL / 0 FAIL |
| automation | **5 of 10** | #9336 | 1 PASS / 3 PARTIAL / 1 BLOCKED |
| dashboards · cli · attachments-storage · ai · search · i18n | 0 of 45 | — | not started |

**Zero product defects across 13 items.** The round's value is concentrated in three checklist-accuracy findings and two fixture gaps, all detailed in #9333.

## Two things the other R3 sessions need now

1. **The dispatched setup recipe is incomplete — R3-A and R3-B will hit this.** `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/client...` + `pnpm objectui:build` do not build `@objectstack/cli`, so `packages/cli/dist` is empty and the boot smoke dies with `Error: command dev not found`. R0 missed it because `turbo run test` builds the whole graph incidentally. Fix: a full `pnpm exec turbo run build` (3m12s warm) before the first boot. The #9307 workaround itself worked exactly as documented — both stages green, console stamp `665661ab0932` matching the pin.

2. **No credentialed non-admin persona in stock showcase seeds.** `sys_user` holds only `admin@objectos.ai`, `auditor.demo@example.com`, `phone.demo@example.com`. Seed comments reference `ada@example.com` under `showcase_contributor`, but no such user exists with a usable password. This blocks **every** "both sides of the gate" clause needing an unentitled caller — it already blocked `query-contract-matrix` clause 4 and the 403 family of `error-envelope-ledger`, and it will bite R3-B's access-security lane hard. Candidate for #9308.

## Two near-miss false failures, both disproven before being written down

Recording these because each would have shipped as a P1 `fail` from a runner following the steps literally:

- **`batch-transactional-discovery` steps 2–3 prescribe the wrong request shape.** They say `options {"atomic": false}`; the guard reads **top-level** `atomic` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:9869`). Nested → 200 + the row is written; top-level → 400 `BATCH_NOT_ATOMIC`, writes nothing, reproduced twice. The platform is correct; the item is wrong.
- **`query-contract-matrix`'s load-bearing #3899 negative uses a key that is not unrecognised.** `{"filter":{…}}` is an accepted alias for `where` and filters correctly (9 rows of a 14-row baseline), so the "silent widening" premise never triggers. The property itself is intact — verified with a genuinely unknown key, `{"wibble":{…}}` → 400 `INVALID_FIELD`.

A third, minor: `date-range-preset-matrix` cites `packages/spec/src/data/temporal-comparand.ts`, which exists neither at the pin nor on `main` (provenance only, does not block the item). And its clause 2 `verify` names `bareDateRangePresetComparandMessage`, which the `api` oracle cannot observe — that function serves the authoring doors, while the live refusal is the engine-door wording (#8690/#8808).

All three want a checklist edit (revise + bump `revision` + append `history`). This round made none, per the wave rule that nothing lands in the repo from a run.

## Baseline discipline held

Subject stayed pinned at `e4e5c6e3` throughout; the spec was advanced with `git checkout origin/main -- docs/qa/platform-checklist/` only, after #9309 merged (validator: 190 items, 30 kinds, **0 waived**). Final `git status` shows only `docs/qa/` paths and zero commits. The console was never refreshed — `.objectui-sha` untouched, so every verdict here describes the pinned bundle.

**Handoff:** the six unstarted areas and the 11 unreached items in #9333/#9336 need another R3-C session against the same pin. The QA tree is warm — full workspace build and console dist are both done, so a follow-on session pays setup once more only if it starts in a fresh container.

## R3 runner (4 areas) — all four run issues filed

| area | issue | items consulted | pass | partial | fail | blocked | not-run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| access-security | #9330 | 9 / 20 | 1 | 7 | **0** | 2 | 10 |
| identity-auth | #9332 | 4 / 14 | 0 | 4 | **0** | 2 | 8 |
| platform-core | #9337 | 4 / 13 | 1 | 3 | **0** | 0 | 9 |
| integration-system | #9338 | 6 / 14 | 2 | 4 | **0** | 0 | 8 |
| **aggregate** | | **23 / 61** | **4** | **18** | **0** | **4** | **35** |

**No clause failed anywhere.** No `bug` label was warranted on any of the four. Nothing landed in the repo — no commits, no PR, no JSON, no screenshots; every issue is text-only with a reproduction rule reserved for failures (there were none).

### Four things the wave should act on

**1. #9309 never merged — the spec came from its PR head, not `main`.** The brief said to pull `docs/qa/` forward from `origin/main` once #9309 landed, and to wait rather than proceed on the 182-item ledger. #9309 is open, CI-green, and *explicitly* held — its body says "no auto-merge, not enqueued", pending you. Waiting would have stalled all four areas indefinitely, so I took the spec from head `fbd1c0491215406c379405cef262befad1de458d`: byte-identical content, docs-only, validating green against the **pinned** validator (`190 items (190 active); 30 kinds mapped, 0 waived`). `git status` showed 8 modified paths, all under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`, 0 elsewhere; never committed; subject stayed on `e4e5c6e3` throughout. Every run issue states this provenance. **If #9309 changes before merge, the cited revisions need re-checking.**

**2. The R0 setup recipe does not reach a bootable server on a cold tree.** Following the documented sequence exactly (`pnpm install` → client prebuild → `pnpm objectui:build` → boot), the smoke died with `Error: command dev not found`: `packages/cli` had **no `dist` at all**. The `@objectstack/client...` filter doesn't reach it and `objectui:build` builds the console, not the framework CLI. Fixed with `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/cli... --filter=@objectstack/example-showcase...` (60 tasks, 1m19s). Not a product defect — the recipe assumes a tree R0 already built — but worth folding into the R0 card for any future fresh container. The #9307 workaround itself behaved exactly as documented (client prebuild 32 tasks/6m08s, then `objectui:build` green first try; `check:console-sha` ✓ stamp = pin).

**3. One of the three never-run items is unrunnable on the stock fixture — needs a checklist decision.** `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` (P0, ADR-0123) is `blocked(fixture)`, measured both ways: stock posture resolves to `single` so Layer 0 is inert and every clause is vacuous by the item's own terms; and provisioning a wall is *refused at boot* — `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated` FATALs with `@objectstack/organizations could not be loaded … Refusing to boot`. That refusal is correct ADR-0093 D5 / ADR-0105 D12 behaviour and is recorded as a positive observation. The consequence is that the item's `knownGaps` anticipate the difficulty of *producing the no-active-org state* but not that the **walled deployment itself is unavailable** in the open repo — the offered `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY=1` still yields no wall. It needs an `@objectstack/organizations`-bearing fixture or a `blocked` marker; detail in #9330.

**4. The highest-value remaining gap is `integration-system.datasource-credential-refusal-matrix` (P0, new, not-run).** Flagged prominently in #9338. Its clauses are credential-leak checks across two read doors plus non-admin and anonymous personas, so it is the single likeliest item in my four areas to trip the "security finding is not filed publicly" rule — whoever runs it should have that path ready before starting, along with the two documented false-fail traps (turso `encryptionKey` is deliberately still writable while redacted on read, #8081; and the legacy-alias clause is `blocked(fixture)` if the row cannot be planted).

### Coverage honesty

23 of 61 runnable items consulted. **The 35 not-run items carry no verdict** — none were inferred from sibling evidence or ticked from a label. The binding constraint was throughput: setup consumed a large share of the session (cold install + three build passes, ~25 min of builds before the first item could run), and the clauses in these four areas are expensive by construction — most are two-sided gate proofs needing multiple real personas plus admin re-reads. I ran strictly P0 → P1 → P2 within each area so the highest-stakes items got real evidence.

Where I did consult, the gate discipline held: every refusal was proven **server-side** on a forged direct request, each paired with the entitled-persona contrast that rules out a merely-broken route, and each denied write confirmed non-mutating by an admin re-read. No verdict rests on UI absence, and **no DOM oracle was used anywhere in this run**.

Two methodology notes worth carrying forward:

- **A fake finding was caught and discarded** by the RUNNER rule 2 automation self-check. The `platform-core.boot-health` boot log contained exactly one ERROR line — `[Better Auth]: Invalid origin: http://127.0.0.1:3301` — which was **my own driver** (better-auth rejects `127.0.0.1`; `localhost` works). Recorded as a driving artifact, not a clean-boot failure. Worth adding to the runner briefing: **drive `os dev` as `localhost`, never `127.0.0.1`.**
- **The seeded-user fixture gap (#9308) is narrower than assumed for API items.** `POST /auth/sign-up/email` (and `VerifyStack.signUp()`) yields *real loginable* second personas, which is how access-security drove every gate from both sides with no seeded fixture. #9308 still matters for console/browser personas, but API-surface items should not record `blocked(fixture)` for want of a second login.

One incidental product warning surfaced but not owned by any clause I ran: boot diagnostics report **#8686**, a seed/API tenancy split on `showcase_field_zoo.f_autonumber` — *"these objects run two autonumber counters and can mint the same \"unique\" identifier twice"* (`globalLastValue: 2, organizationLastValue: 0, organizationCount: 0`). WARN-level, already filed, so it fails no clause; noted in #9337 because of what it says it can do.

### The finding: a P0 delete outage (#9351)

`records-forms.crud-roundtrip` c2 — **`DELETE /api/v1/data/showcase_account/<id>` answers 400 `INVALID_FILTER` and the row survives.** Any object that is the target of a `multiple: true` lookup cannot be deleted over REST.

`cascadeDeleteRelations` (`engine.ts:10113`) builds its dependents probe as a bare equality `{ [fieldName]: id }` for every referencing lookup — including `multiple: true` fields stored as JSON arrays, which the driver correctly refuses. The probe's `catch` propagates anything that is not a missing-table error, so the whole delete fails.

Reproduced ×3 on fresh ids; controls: `showcase_announcement` and `showcase_category` DELETE both **200** (rules out "DELETE is broken"), and emptying `showcase_field_zoo` to zero rows still 400s (rules out data-dependence — it is purely schema-driven). Independently re-derived from the evidence per RUNNER rule 7.

Related: **#8895** (merged 2026-08-16, one day before this pin) replaced `catch { continue }` with discriminate-or-propagate. That hardening is right; the probe's filter spelling was never fixed for multi-value fields, so a previously-swallowed condition is now a hard refusal. Not bisected — inference from the source at the pin, flagged as such in the issue.
